correctness.rationale: For all N>=3, H(s^i)-H(s)=2J(tau_{i-1}+tau_i+tau_{i+1}), so strictly blocked tau words have pairwise defects separated by at least 3 cyclic sites. The spin-to-tau GF(2) map has kernel dimension 0 unless 3 divides N, when its kernel is exactly the four 3-periodic bit solutions; image is characterized by equality of the three mod-3 defect parities. A 3-state cyclic transfer matrix counts admissible tau words and three sign characters enforce the image; this proves both polynomial cases with no asymptotic or finite-experiment assumption. Exact low-energy multiplicities and the plastic-root second growth term follow analytically. The independent direct-Hamiltonian checker exhaustively compared 65,528 spin states through N=15 and additional cyclic defect cases to N=24; finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The original statement that local tau defects must be separated does not determine the number of realizable periodic spin configurations: for length six there are ten abstract admissible cyclic defect strings but sixteen blocked spin states because admissibility and multiplicity depend on congruence-parity constraints. Its leading asymptotic cannot imply the exact finite-volume spin polynomial or the non-leading correction. Broader Edwards-ensemble formulas in [2] apply to different kinetic constraints, and [3] considers random pair interactions.

value.rationale: The classic three-body glassy chain was studied through its exponential metastable entropy, but finite periodic samples have global compatibility sectors that alter the actual physical-spin census. The exact all-length blocked-energy generating polynomial simultaneously explains why the one-defect band disappears at lengths divisible by three, gives its replacement first-excitation multiplicity, and quantifies a previously unexposed subleading exponential commensurability term while retaining the known leading entropy. This is a natural complete finite-volume classification and a useful benchmark for kinetic freezing and Edwards-ensemble enumeration, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
